name: pixel-measure
desc: Free, open-source screen ruler for Windows — measure pixels, spacing and angles over any app. 100 MB portable, offline, no account, MIT.
features: ✅ **Pixel-exact ruler** — horizontal, vertical and free-angle rulers snap to pixel edges over any window
✅ **Magnifier loupe** — 4x to 16x zoom with a crosshair grid for picking exact boundaries
✅ **Guides and markers** — drop persistent guide lines to check alignment across a design or build
✅ **Click-through mode** — rulers stay visible but pass clicks to the app underneath, so nothing is blocked
✅ **Multi-monitor and DPI aware** — per-monitor scaling handled; measurements stay true at 125 percent and 150 percent
✅ **Copy measurements** — one hotkey copies position, size and distance values as text
✅ **100 MB self-contained exe** — runtime bundled, portable, offline, MIT with SHA-256 releases
compare: | Feature | **pixel-measure** | Screen Calipers | JR Screen Ruler | Pixel Ruler |
| Multi-monitor DPI aware | **Yes** | Partial | No | No |
| Portable, no install | **Yes, 100 MB** | Installer | Zip | Installer |
faqQ: how to measure pixels on screen in Windows?
faqA: There is no built-in ruler beyond Paint tricks, and freeware rulers were built for 96 DPI single monitors and drift on modern scaling. pixel-measure is DPI-aware per monitor, adds a magnifier for exact edge picking, and its click-through mode never blocks the app below. It is a 100 MB portable exe, MIT, fully offline.
s1: Dark overlay ruler (accent amber #F59E0B): 384 px span marked, tick labels every 10 px, mm toggle, readout chip showing X 128, Y 640.
s2: Magnifier loupe at 16x with crosshair grid centered on a button edge, pixel color coordinates below, freeze-frame toggle on.
s3: Settings: units px or mm, opacity slider at 80 percent, hotkey list, click-through toggle highlighted, per-monitor DPI status cards.
